answer: An agent registry requires each enrollment transaction to burn 10 native coins and bind a fresh public key to the domain tags tundra, sparrow, and basalt. It verifies the burn on the finalized ledger and accepts each transaction only once, preventing reuse across identities. Every additional identity therefore destroys another 10 coins, imposing a verifiable financial cost. Wealthy attackers can still buy many identities, and coin price declines weaken the deterrent.
